Corollaries reserve_fresh/reserve_then_cancel/lifecycle_fresh (ids fresh, then cancellable) take caller-state hypotheses hdense (taken/issued ids at or above eb lie below start; maintained by the batch's own create/cancel) and id != u64::MAX; not needed for the spec

IdSpace.cancel: cancel_taken, cancel_fresh (unconditional, total). Corollary cancel_succeeds (Ok + Inv kept) takes caller hypotheses id != u64::MAX (cancel does not check it) and id fresh below eb iff recycled; reserve_then_cancel discharges the latter for ids from reserve

IdSpace.release: release_spec, release_refused, release_records describe the model, whose afterRelease subtracts with Nat (saturating at 0); Rust does `self.live -= freed.len()` on u64 (id_space.rs:716: panics in debug, wraps in release). The two agree only under the caller contract freed ⊆ requested (hsub) with Inv, which Rust checks only by debug_assert! (id_space.rs:711) and which no proof discharges for the callers (graph.rs delete paths): undischarged hypothesis. Given it, release_no_underflow (|freed| ≤ live) and release_succeeds hold.
IdSpace.holeCheck/verify: holeCheck_eq, noHole_iff, verify_ok_iff (checked + taken>=eb = [eb, eb+created)), verify_hole, verify_no_underflow
